description: Named stress scenarios for the fictional restaurant in restaurant_business.json (issue #109). SYNTHETIC / ILLUSTRATIVE: invented deterministic stress paths that use only the MATH_MODEL §1 shock channels (demand, rate, supplier outage). Not forecasts and not based on any real company or real event. Hand checks: docs/MATH_MODEL.md §10b.

scenarios.name: Road closure: -30% covers for 9 weeks, 3-week recovery
scenarios.rationale: Street works close the road and parking outside the restaurant in weeks 4-12, so covers fall by 30%, then return over 3 weeks; each lost sales dollar costs the 66% gross margin.

shock.name: Road closure: -30% covers for 9 weeks, 3-week recovery

scenarios.name: Distributor loss: main protein/produce distributor out for 4 weeks
scenarios.rationale: The main broadline distributor stops delivering in weeks 6-9, so the 60% of menu sales that need its proteins and produce are lost unless the restaurant buys from a backup supplier at a 15% premium.

shock.name: Distributor loss: main protein/produce distributor out for 4 weeks

scenarios.name: Slow season + rate rise: -30% covers in weeks 2-9, +300bp from week 1
scenarios.rationale: A seasonal lull cuts covers by 30% for 8 weeks while the lender reprices the floating loan by 3 points (156,000 x 3% / 52 = 90 more interest per week); the dip is deep but cash recovers slowly afterwards.

shock.name: Slow season + rate rise: -30% covers in weeks 2-9, +300bp from week 1
